title: Design small-prime packed kernel strategy
description:
Select the strategy for GF(7), GF(31), and GF(251) performance parity.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] The design compares packed residues, tables, SIMD lanes, and fflas-style modular tricks.
- [hard] One strategy is selected with feasibility evidence for each in-scope prime, scoped per the per-prime maturity marker policy in `CLAUDE.md` § *Success-criterion maturity markers*. The selected strategy must be feasibility-evidenced against either the `[hard]` 1.5×-of-fflas absolute target or, if the AVX2-host envelope is structurally shorter than that target, against an `[aspirational]` per-host envelope target with the empirical evidence recorded in the linked design document.

## Amendment — 2026-05-05 (user-approved, Path A)

The original criterion #2 wording was "One strategy is selected with feasibility evidence" without the per-prime maturity-marker scoping. The amended wording above was approved by the user during 5cacaec5's R3 review cycle (AskUserQuestion: "Issue 5cacaec5 design has hit an R2 code-review fail with a real architectural blocker") in favour of Option A: *"Accept C + amend GF(251) target now"*. The amendment is recorded as a visible note here per the project's amendment-log convention, mirroring the Wave-3 user decisions on `9a715d75` proposal #1 and `a3412e15` sparse exclusions.

**Empirical basis for the amendment.** The architect's design at `dev/plans/small_prime_kernel_strategy.md` § 6 #2 quantifies the AVX2 16-bit-MAC throughput envelope on the pinned bench host (Zen-3, no AVX-512) at 80 Gop/s. The downstream `662f7a15` 1.5× absolute targets per `dev/plans/sota_target_matrix.md` § 5.1 are GF(7) ≈ 33.5 Gop/s (42 % of peak — clearly feasible), GF(31) ≈ 33.5 Gop/s (same envelope), GF(251) ≈ 85.3 Gop/s (107 % of peak — structurally beyond AVX2-only integer SIMD; fflas reaches its 128 Gop/s baseline only via Modular<float> + OpenBLAS sgemm, Candidate D in the design). The amendment permits the design to select Candidate C with `[hard]` feasibility evidence for GF(7) + GF(31) and `[aspirational]` per-host-envelope evidence for GF(251), instead of forcing a Candidate D selection that would break the project's pure-Rust posture.

**Downstream consequence.** `662f7a15`'s description was amended in the same commit chain to mark its GF(251) success-criterion row as `[aspirational]` with a re-escalation threshold (~3.2× of fflas, i.e. ≤ 40 Gop/s, at which the implementation re-escalates the amendment with the measured number).
